competitive_landscape: The Ionian is served today by conventional ferry operators and seasonal day-trip boats running fixed, weather-exposed schedules, with much inter-island travel still routed by road plus a short crossing. The volume and growth are real demand proof; the slow, fragmented, diesel status quo is the experience we improve on. No foiling operator runs here.

regulatory_note: Greek flag / EU; Hellenic Coast Guard certification and Greek cabotage rules favour EU-flagged vessels. Berths sit at established marinas and port funds (Gouvia Marina, Corfu and Lefkada port authorities). EU maritime-decarbonisation policy adds a clean-fleet tailwind; the Corfu↔Brindisi leg additionally touches Italian port and immigration authorities.
seasonality: The Ionian's defining advantage is shelter: it sits west of the meltemi (etesian) NW summer wind that batters the Aegean, so its protected channels stay calm far more of the year. Where afternoon chop does build, foiling flight above the surface keeps the ride smooth and the schedule reliable — extending the workable season at both shoulders.

summary: The Ionian Islands are the calm, green counterpoint to the Cyclades: Corfu, Paxos, Lefkada, Kefalonia and Zakynthos sit in a sheltered north-south chain west of the meltemi wind belt, strung together by short hops that almost all fall inside all-electric range. It is the fastest-growing Greek tourism region, with double-digit early-2026 arrivals growth, yet inter-island travel still depends on slow conventional ferries and long road-plus-ferry detours. A foiling spine down the Ionian turns a fragmented chain into one smooth, near-silent corridor on water that stays workable far more of the year than the open Aegean.
tagline: The protected-water spine of Greece's fastest-growing island region — short, sheltered hops the meltemi never reaches.
